promotion.title: Leave-usage promotion (when unused leave is not paid)
promotion.description: If the employer follows the written procedure of LSA Article 61 exactly, leave the employee still does not use expires without an allowance.
steps: Within 10 days from 6 months before the leave period ends, the employer notifies remaining days in writing and asks the employee to set dates
The employee sets dates and notifies the employer within 10 days
If the employee does not, the employer designates dates in writing by 2 months before the period ends

Monthly leave in the first year: request within 10 days from 3 months before the 1-year mark, designate by 1 month before (leave arising after the request: request within 5 days from 1 month before, designate by 10 days before)
If all steps were followed, unused leave expires with no allowance
promotion.warning: Verbal notice alone, or letting the employee work on the designated leave day, may invalidate the procedure. Leave left unused because of resignation is paid regardless.

hourlyLeave.title: Annual leave by the hour
hourlyLeave.before: From Jun 10, 2027, if a worker requests annual leave split into hours, the employer must grant it. The hourly unit and the day limit will be set by Enforcement Decree (reflected once final). Dismissal or other unfavorable treatment for requesting or using leave is also banned (new LSA Art. 60(5) and (9), Act No. 21784).
hourlyLeave.after: If a worker requests annual leave split into hours, the employer must grant it (LSA Art. 60(5), effective Jun 10, 2027). The hourly unit and the day limit are set by the LSA Enforcement Decree. Dismissal or other unfavorable treatment for requesting or using leave is banned (Art. 60(9)).

basis.title: Hire-date basis vs fiscal-year basis
items: Hire-date basis (the legal rule): leave is granted on each work anniversary — 15 days at 1 year, 16 at 3 years, 17 at 5 years, and so on.
Fiscal-year basis: everyone receives leave on January 1. The first January 1 after hire gives prorated leave (15 × days worked in the hire year ÷ 365), then 15 days from the next January 1.
The fiscal-year basis is allowed for administrative convenience if the rules of employment provide for it, but it must not disadvantage employees.
When you leave, leave is recalculated on the hire-date basis; if the fiscal-year basis gave fewer days, the difference is paid as leave allowance (MOEL guidance).
If you joined on January 1, both bases give the same result.

smallBiz.title: No statutory annual leave for workplaces under 5 employees or very short part-time workers
smallBiz.body: Article 60 does not apply to workplaces with 4 or fewer regular employees (LSA Enforcement Decree, Annex 1). Workers averaging under 15 hours a week over 4 weeks also have no annual leave (Art. 18(3)). Company rules or contracts that grant leave still apply.

rules.title: Accrual rules (LSA Article 60)
items: Under 1 year (or attendance below 80%): 1 day per month of perfect attendance, up to 11 days, usable until the 1-year mark
3+ years of service: +1 day every 2 years beyond the first year (16 at 3 years, 17 at 5 years … capped at 25 from 21 years)
Up to 26 days in the first two years (11 monthly + 15 at the first anniversary)
Annual leave is usable for 1 year from the grant date; unused days can be claimed in cash (3-year wage claim limitation)
You must still be employed on the first anniversary itself to receive the 15 days (Supreme Court 2021Da227100)

tips.title: Notes
items: Unused leave can be paid out as leave allowance
Company policies may vary from statutory minimum
Leave promotion system may exempt unused leave pay
Parental leave period counts as attendance

whatIs.title: What is the Annual Leave Calculator?
whatIs.description: The annual leave calculator automatically computes how many paid vacation days (연차 유급휴가) have accrued based on your hire date, following the Korean Labor Standards Act. It handles both the monthly accrual system for employees with less than 1 year of service and the annual grant system with seniority bonuses for long-tenured employees. Enter days already used to see your remaining balance.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select your hire date — your tenure and accrued leave days are automatically calculated.
2. Enter the number of leave days already used to see your remaining balance.
3. For employees under 1 year, monthly accrual (1 day/month) is shown separately.
4. Check the leave expiry date to plan usage before days are forfeited.

items.q: How much leave do I get in my first year?
items.a: 1 day per month of perfect attendance, up to 11 days, then 15 days on your first anniversary — up to 26 days over two years. Monthly leave must be used before the 1-year mark.

items.q: If I work exactly one year and leave, do I get 15 days?
items.a: No. Per Supreme Court 2021Da227100 and MOEL guidance (Dec 2021), you must still be employed on the day after completing one year (the anniversary). Hired 2025-03-02 and last day 2026-03-01: 11 days only; last day 2026-03-02: 11 + 15.

items.q: How does leave grow after 3 years?
items.a: +1 day every 2 years beyond the first year: 16 days at 3–4 years, 17 at 5–6 … 24 at 19–20, capped at 25 from 21 years.

items.q: What happens to leave I don't use?
items.a: It expires after its 1-year usage period, but you can claim an allowance for unused days — unless the employer properly followed the Article 61 promotion procedure in writing.

Unused days × daily ordinary wage. Monthly: monthly ordinary wage ÷ 209 h × 8 h. Hourly: hourly wage × daily contractual hours. Rules of employment may use average wage. It is taxable and must be paid within 14 days of leaving (Art. 36).

items.q: My company uses the fiscal-year basis. Do I lose out when I leave?
items.a: You should not. On leaving, leave is recalculated on the hire-date basis and any shortfall is paid. Set the reference date to your last day and turn on 'I leave on this date' to see the difference.

items.q: Do small businesses or part-timers get annual leave?
items.a: Workplaces with 4 or fewer regular employees are exempt. Part-timers at larger workplaces working 15+ hours a week get leave prorated by hours (full-time leave days × part-time hours ÷ full-time hours × 8 hours, rounding up to whole hours — Enforcement Decree Appendix 2).

items.q: Does parental or maternity leave count?
items.a: Yes. Maternity leave, parental leave and time off for work injury count as attendance (Art. 60).
